description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of experts across 24 layers in a multilingual large language model architecture, as described in the paper “Less, but Better: Efficient Multilingual Expansion for LLMs via Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Experts,” ranges from 0 to 10, indicating the total count of experts assigned per layer. The horizontal axis represents the 24 model layers, numbered 1 through 24. Each bar is a stacked column composed of three segments: blue (G0), green (G1), and yellow (G2), corresponding to three expert groups as defined in the legend. The height of each bar reflects the total number of experts per layer, while the color segments show the contribution of each group. For example, layer 1 has 9 total experts (1 from G0, 4 from G1, and 4 from G2), while layer 7 has only 3 experts (1 from G0, 1 from G1, and 1 from G2). The distribution is not uniform: early layers (e.g., 1–5) and later layers (e.g., 19–22) tend to have more experts, while middle layers (e.g., 10–15) are sparser. The chart visually supports the paper’s theme of efficient expansion by showing how expert allocation varies per layer, potentially reflecting task-specific or language-specific demands.
